claims.text: Lithographic patterning reduces the lateral dimensions of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films to form nanoscale nanoribbons.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films have bulk-like microstructural characteristics.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films have bulk-like magnetic-domain characteristics.
Reducing the films to nanoscale nanoribbons imposes finite-size constraints.
Nanoribbon confinement modifies magnetic-domain dynamics.
Nanoribbon edges induce domain-wall pinning.
The higher surface-to-volume ratio of patterned nanoribbons enhances interfacial effects.
Finite-size confinement restricts the evolution and motion of magnetic domains.
Restricted magnetic-domain motion limits the entropy change during magnetization reversal.
Restricted domain motion increases energy dissipation and magnetic hysteresis.
Patterning into nanoribbons lowers the peak magnetocaloric response relative to non-patterned thin films.
Patterning into nanoribbons increases or broadens the hysteresis width during low-field cycles.
The altered surface-to-volume ratio changes the effective heat-transfer rate.
Decreasing the sample dimensions can favor faster heat removal.
Cooling performance becomes constrained by heat transfer when cycling frequencies approach the thermal-diffusion limit.
Nanoribbons exhibit a more pronounced frequency dependence of magnetocaloric response near the thermal-dissipation limit than non-patterned films.
The proposed behavior applies near the magnetic transition temperature under low applied magnetic fields.
The proposed behavior applies when nanoribbon lateral dimensions are below the material's bulk characteristic length scales.
Enhanced heat dissipation in confined geometries may partly offset the effect of reduced domain mobility.
Edge quality and pattern uniformity may alter the measured magnetocaloric and hysteretic behavior.
